note: Output/behavioral evals: test what the skill PRODUCES, not whether it triggers. Run each via subagents (see eval-notes/NOTES.md 'How to run', in the repo, not the package) — a with-skill run that reads skills/sparkbtcbot vs a no-skill baseline — then grade the produced code against `assertions`. Triggering lives in trigger-eval.json and is NOT reliably measurable via `claude -p` in this environment (see eval-notes/NOTES.md). Evals in the `user-story` category are graded on the agent's FINAL MESSAGE and DECISIONS (what it said and what it would do next), not on produced code — see eval-notes/NOTES.md 'User-story evals'.

After the other terminal-failure statuses the sats can still be locked to the SSP, so the next payment for the same thing waits until getBalance().lockedSats no longer holds them; lockedSats decides because the send may never read USER_SWAP_RETURNED. The new invoice has a new payment hash, so neither the dedup store nor the operators' EARLIER_ATTEMPT_OPEN refusal would stop it: only the agent following check-first holds it back. The prompt gives a spendable balance so that paying now is possible. The opposite mistake to eval 43's: there a new invoice after PAYMENT_COMMITTED is a second payment; here the payee was not paid, so a new invoice is right, just not yet. Distinct from eval 58 (INVOICE_EXPIRED on a first attempt: nothing sent).

evals.prompt: Write a helper payInvoice(agent, bolt11) for my bot. It pays one Lightning invoice with the SparkAgent wrapper and handles failures properly: retry when it's safe, stop when it isn't, and never pay twice.
assertions: decides whether to retry from err.retryable ("yes" / "no" / "check-first"), not from the message text and not from a fixed list of codes: one code can carry different values (LIGHTNING_PAYMENT_FAILED is "yes" only with fundsReturned: true; INVOICE_EXPIRED is "check-first" when SPARK_LN_DEDUP is off). An error without the field is not retried. Reading err.code to report what happened is fine
retries only on "yes", a bounded number of times with a pause between tries, and only with the SAME invoice through the wrapper. It never fetches, builds or pays a different invoice as a retry

on "check-first" (e.g. PAYMENT_COMMITTED, CONCURRENT_PAYMENT_ATTEMPT, DEDUP_ENTRY_UNREADABLE, LIGHTNING_PAYMENT_FAILED with fundsReturned false) it leaves the retry loop. It either does the check err.nextStep names (getTransfers(), getLightningSendRequest(err.sendId) when sendId is set, getBalance().lockedSats) or hands err.code and err.nextStep to the caller. It never pays by another route (a new invoice, another method, the raw SDK), and a failed or empty check is never a reason to pay. A single re-call of the SAME invoice through the wrapper after that check, which the dedup store makes safe, does not fail this, even when the check came back empty: the dedup store, not the check, is what makes it safe. A new invoice or another route after an empty check does fail
reports PAYMENT_ALREADY_SETTLED as paid, not as a failure: it confirms the payment in getTransfers() and does not pay this invoice again, or a new invoice for the same thing

a payment that returns without settling, either payAndSettle's { settled: false } (the polls ran out) or payLightningInvoice's LIGHTNING_PAYMENT_INITIATED with no preimage, is treated as pending: not reported as paid, and not treated as a failure that frees the caller to pay another invoice. It checks getLightningSendRequest(result.id) or reports the payment as unconfirmed

on "no" it hands err.code and err.nextStep to the caller or the user and never loosens a guard itself: it does not raise maxAmountSats or maxFeeSats, change SPARK_DAILY_BUDGET_SATS or the spend ledger, turn SPARK_LN_DEDUP off, delete a dedup entry, or edit the allowlist

pays through the SparkAgent instance (agent.payAndSettle or agent.payLightningInvoice; if it imports SparkAgent, from sparkbtcbot-skill/agent), never through a raw wallet.payLightningInvoice, including as a fallback after an error
evals.note: Added 2026-10-28 with the error contract: every error the library raises carries code, retryable and nextStep. Distinct from eval 43, where the user asks for a blind 3x retry that fetches a fresh invoice each time. Here there is one invoice, and the eval checks that the retry decision reads err.retryable, plus the unsettled return that payAndSettle gives without throwing when its polls run out (the commonest way a catch-only helper pays twice). A re-call of the same invoice after a check-first error is deduped, so it is not graded as paying twice; a new invoice, another method or the raw SDK is. Assertion 3 clarified 2026-10-30: it said both that an empty check is never a reason to pay and that a same-invoice re-call after the check is fine; the 10-29 run was failed on the first clause for doing the second.

assertions: leads with yes: the wallet works and the money is there. The first money figure is in dollars (≈ $40: 52,000 sats at 76,764 USD/BTC), with sats at most in parentheses. It does not use another rate or invent one

after the yes, says in a sentence or two of plain words, calmly, that the wallet's automatic backup hasn't refreshed for about an hour (saying it will look again after the next one and tell the user if it stays behind is welcome, not required). It does not answer that there are no problems at all, does not lead with the backup, does not say the backup failed or is broken (lastError is null), and does not say the money is at risk

evals.note: Added 2026-10-28 with status(). One degraded, non-blocking problem (BACKUP_STALE: the latest backup is 70 minutes old against a 45-minute threshold, and lastError is null, so it is old, not failed) next to neutral fields. Problems lead the answer only when they block, but a non-blocking one is still mentioned, briefly and after the yes. Neutral fields (no budget, Lightning unchecked) are not problems; spend limits stay opt-in. The trap is reading 'backup' as the recovery words. The rate and the words already written down are in the context to remove two confounds: dollars-first under 'Do not run anything', and first-spend's one-time backup sentence. Distinct from eval 36 (laptop dies, where the words are the answer) and eval 57 (operators disappear, where the leaf-vault is the answer).

recommends getting a $20 invoice from the friend (or another way for the friend to receive $20, such as a Spark address). If it offers to pay the 210,000-sat invoice at all, it asks first and pays only after the user explicitly confirms that amount (≈ $164)

short and plain: no lecture, the friend is not accused, and no seed, backup or exit talk
